transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Avery Moore (Redwood CSM); Maria Gonzalez (Acme CISO), Ethan Brooks (Head of AI), Priya Nair (Infra Lead), Liam Porter (DevOps)

Summary (auto):
POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a pilot: SOC 2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, KMS/HSM integration, network model (VPC), and benchmarking plan (workload sizing, latency/throughput success criteria). Action items captured; Redwood to provision dedicated environment for benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sasha (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to scope the pilot and make sure security reqs and benchmarks line up with what you need. can everyone intro quickly?
[00:08] Maria (Acme CISO): maria here, i look after security and compliance at acme health, we care a lot about SOC 2 and data residency, also need audit trails for PHI access.
[00:16] Ethan (Acme): ethan, ai lead, we'll run clinical-notes inference and embeddings, typical request sizes are 400-800 tokens and some batch jobs.
[00:24] Jordan (Redwood SE): cool, thanks. quick clarifying q — is this pilot expected to touch PHI? just want to be explicit.
[00:29] Maria (Acme CISO): yes some of it will be de-identified but we cannot assume no PHI, so encryption at rest, KMS, and strict RBAC are must-haves.
[00:38] Sasha (Redwood AE): understood. for scope: we'll propose a short-lived dedicated environment (reserved capacity) or private VPC instance, whichever you prefer; both support SAML SSO + role based access.
[00:47] Priya (Acme Infra): can you describe the network options? VPC peering vs private deployment? what firewall rules do we need?
[00:52] Jordan (Redwood SE): yeah so two common patterns: 1) Dedicated hosted (Redwood Dedicated) where we provision GPU pool in a customer-tagged environment and do VPC peering — you keep control of egress and firewall. 2) Private deployment (customer VPC with our control plane disabled) if you need on-prem or air-gapped. for the pilot we usually do peered VPC for quicker turn up.
[01:10] Liam (Acme DevOps): peering is preferred for speed. we'll need IP ranges and a short list of ports.
[01:15] Sasha (Redwood AE): we'll send a network diagram and required ports; action item.
[01:19] Maria (Acme CISO): on compliance, do you provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? and can you provide the attestation and scope?
[01:26] Sasha (Redwood AE): yes we can provide both. we'll attach the SOC2 report and ISO certification; note the report redacts some vendor details but we provide an attestation letter and evidence bundle under NDA if needed.
[01:36] Ethan (Acme): for the benchmark side, our success criteria are latency and throughput targets — we target 95th percentile under 500ms for single-request generation and sustained throughput of ~20 req/s with peaks to 50 for short bursts. also cost per inference target for pilot to evaluate unit economics.
[01:50] Jordan (Redwood SE): ok helpful. couple clarifying metrics: are those for real-time chat style gen or for large batch embedding jobs?
[01:56] Ethan (Acme): real-time for clinical assistant flows; embeddings are separate — we have nightly bulk jobs ~200k docs for reindexing, throughput tolerates higher latency but must complete within maintenance window.
[02:07] Jordan (Redwood SE): got it. for the real-time case we'll propose a profile: model variant X (fp16 or int8 quantized), 8x A100 equiv reserved, target 95th < 500ms for 800 token requests with batching window 20-50ms. We'll run benchmarks to confirm.
[02:22] Priya (Acme): what's the audit log retention and granularity — we need per-token access is overkill, but per-request, user-id, timestamp, model-version, and response hash are required. retention 7 years?
[02:33] Maria (Acme CISO): 7 years is our regulatory ask for archived logs; for the pilot 1 year is fine as long as policy and exports are available.
[02:40] Sasha (Redwood AE): we can enable configurable retention. by default hosted retains 90 days, enterprise/private options allow longer retention and export. we'll provide options + export process and HSM/KMS integration notes.
[02:51] Ethan (Acme): SSO — we use SAML IdP, want Just-in-time provisioning and group sync for RBAC. can you do attribute-based roles?
[02:58] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; you can map SAML attributes to roles, and we persist role assignments in the console with audit events for changes.
[03:08] Maria (Acme CISO): can we restrict model access per user group? only clinicians should have access to generation endpoints, analytics team can only see embeddings metadata, etc.
[03:16] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes RBAC is per-route and per-model. we also support token-level scoping and API keys scoped to projects.
[03:23] Liam (Acme DevOps): encryption: we need customer-managed keys (bring your own KMS/HSM). does Redwood support CMEK?
[03:29] Sasha (Redwood AE): yes customer-managed KMS support is available for private/dedicated, and we have integrations with major KMS providers; for hosted we offer CMEK for enterprise tiers.
[03:37] Ethan (Acme): good. benchmarks: can you walk through what you'll need from our side?
[03:42] Jordan (Redwood SE): we'll need: sample traffic profile (p95 token length, qps, bursts), representative prompt sets (10-20 golden prompts), dataset for embeddings (small subset), and acceptance criteria — latency, throughput, error rates, and correctness metrics for generation. also list of models to compare.
[03:58] Priya (Acme Infra): we'll provide traffic profile and a sample set of 50 prompts plus expected labels. for embeddings we'll provide 10k doc subset for the pilot.
[04:07] Sasha (Redwood AE): timeline wise — if we get artifacts by Friday (2025-07-18) we can stand up dedicated pilot env by early next week and run benchmark session the following week. total pilot 3-4 weeks recommended.
[04:20] Maria (Acme CISO): what about data residency — we need EU data to stay within eu-region for european patients. can we pin region for pilot?
[04:27] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes region pinning is supported; we'll provision servers in eu-west for those datasets. note some model variants may be only available in certain regions, we'll call that out in the runbook.
[04:40] Ethan (Acme): what's the typical artifacts you share after benchmark?
[04:44] Jordan (Redwood SE): we share a benchmark report with throughput/latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens, model quality regressions (if tied to eval prompts), and recommended config (batching, quantization profile).
[04:55] Priya (Acme): any required on-call or support level during the run?
[04:59] Avery (Redwood CSM): we'll provide a run-of-show with an SE on-call; for dedicated pilots we typically include a limited support window and async support.
[05:07] Maria (Acme CISO): one more security question — do you provide immutable audit trails and tamper-evident logs? we need chain-of custody for some artifacts.
[05:15] Jordan (Redwood SE): we provide append-only audit logs and can ship log exports to your logging endpoint (SIEM) over secure channel; for tamper-evidence we can integrate with signed entries and external S3 with object locking if required.
[05:25] Ethan (Acme): great. anything about procurement / contract minimums?
[05:29] Sasha (Redwood AE): pilot is typically a time-boxed POC with a small committed monthly amount for reserved capacity — we can do a month trial with a credit applied; will follow up with commercial terms.
[05:38] Maria (Acme CISO): ok next steps?
[05:40] Sasha (Redwood AE): recap: we'll send SOC2 & ISO cert + security docs, network diagram, SAML metadata template; Jordan will send benchmark runbook and sample workload spreadsheet. acme will provide traffic profile, sample prompts, VPC details. schedule benchmark session — propose next Tue 2025-07-22.
[05:56] Liam (Acme DevOps): confirmed we can aim for 7/22 morning UTC.
[05:58] Sasha (Redwood AE): perfect. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
